title: auto-generate-model-readme-with-telemetry-driven-impact-blurbs
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add automated model README generator that synthesizes onboarding README.md and concise release bullets from model profile, eval highlights, and live telemetry. Improves cross-team discoverability and reduces manual release-note churn.
description:
Motivation: Onboarding teams spend time writing the same boilerplate README and release bullets for every model intake. This PR adds a generator that produces a compact model README.md and a concise impact blurb synthesized from three inputs: the model profile metadata, recent performance/eval snapshots, and aggregated usage telemetry (if available). The generated README covers summary, performance profile, rollout recommendations, known limitations, and example API snippets. It also emits 3-4 release bullets suitable for changelogs or product briefings.

What this changes (summary): commit: 1) introduce generator service and CLI glue (model_registry/tools/readme_generator.py), 2) add templates and formatters (templates/auto_readme/*), 3) add telemetry summarizer hook (model_registry/telemetry/summary_adapter.py), 4) integrate generation into onboarding pipeline (hooks/onboard_postprocess.go), 5) tests and sample fixtures (tests/readme_gen_test.py, fixtures/sample_profile.json).

Why telemetry: When telemetry is present (usage by endpoint, median latency, error-rate by route), the generator includes an "impact score" computed from request volume and latency regression that surfaces which downstream surfaces are likely to be affected by model changes. This helps PMs and SREs prioritize rollouts. Telemetry is optional for privacy; generator falls back to profile-only output.

Generated README sketch (excerpt):
- Title: Compact human-readable model brief
- One-line summary: "ggml-turbo-3b — tuned for chat with 128k context, optimized 8-bit kernels"
- Key metrics: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec baseline, embedding dims, typical seq-length budget
- Perf profile: recommended batch sizing, quantization candidate (int8-fast), expected memory footprint on A100/RTX6000
- Rollout advice: canary 5% for 24h then 25% if no regressions; fallback to model:ggml-turbo-3b-v1 on error
- Known limitations: hallucination cases with numeric reasoning; degrade gracefully with reranker
- Release bullets (automatically composed):
  * Add ggml-turbo-3b-v2: +15% throughput for short prompts; see perf-profile section.
  * Default rollout: canary 5% for 24h (auto-generated recommendation).
  * Telemetry: alerts recommended on latency +30% or error-rate +1.5x baseline.

Files changed (high-level):
- model_registry/tools/readme_generator.py — core generator logic and templating.
- templates/auto_readme/* — handlebars-like templates for README sections and bullets.
- model_registry/telemetry/summary_adapter.py — small adapter to compute traffic-weighted impact score.
- hooks/onboard_postprocess.go — calls generator after profile upload; writes README.md into model bundle.
- tests/readme_gen_test.py — unit tests for template output and telemetry fallback.
- fixtures/sample_profile.json — synthetic model profile used in tests.
- docs/processes/model-onboard.md — document referencing the new auto-generation step.

Commits (high-level):
- c1f4b1d introduce generator skeleton and CLI
- a8d9e02 add telemetry summarizer and impact scoring
- b3e7f44 add templates and README examples
- e91c2fa integrate generator into onboard pipeline (hook)
- f55d6a1 tests, fixtures, and small lint fixes

Review conversation (highlights):
- Liam O'Connor (review): "Love the UX. Two asks: (1) make sure sensitive telemetry is always aggregated (no user IDs), (2) make the rollout suggestions opt-outable in admin UI."
- Maya (author): "Agreed on aggregation, added an explicit aggregation step in summary_adapter.py and documented admin toggle in docs/processes/model-onboard.md."
- Sofia Patel (review): "Can we keep the generated README under model bundle but not auto-publish to public docs?"
- Maya: "Generator writes README.md to the model bundle; publishing to the docs site is a separate pipeline step and left disabled by default."
- Arjun Singh (approval): "Tests look good; nit: simplify the template for the perf table."
- Final: after one small template refactor we got approval from all reviewers.

CI/Checks: Unit tests ran in CI; one flaky test (tests/storage/test_upload) failed on first run and was retried; subsequent run passed. Linting required two small formatting fixes applied in f55d6a1. Integration smoke test (onboard pipeline against a synthetic profile) executed in staging and validated README.md generation.

Backward compatibility and safety: The new hook is behind a feature flag (model.readme_generation.enabled) and defaults to false in existing clusters. The onboarding CLI exposes a --generate-readme flag for early adopters. No public API changes.

Operational notes: The impact score calculation uses a decay window of 14 days by default and can be configured per-organization. Telemetry ingestion adheres to existing aggregation and PII-stripping contracts; nothing with raw user identifiers is persisted in the README.

Testing & QA: Added unit tests to validate template placeholders and telemetry fallback. Added an integration sanity check in the onboard pipeline that writes the README to a temp bundle and asserts presence of the key sections. QA run notes included in the PR thread (passed staging run on 2025-10-06).

Merge: Squash-and-merge after approvals. Merged by Maya on 2025-10-07.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-7702 Add an API endpoint for previewing generated README from UI.
- ENG-7714 Add translation/localization support for generated bulleted release notes.
- PM action: decide default feature-flag rollout policy for orgs.

Notes for docs owners: docs/processes/model-onboard.md updated with the new step and instructions to opt-in via CLI or org flag. Please review and incorporate into the public onboarding guide when product approves.
notes: Merged via squash; changelog added to release-candidate. Feature behind flag; opt-in for 0.3 rollout.
